findings.claim: The newest-first balance check for a record runs only when the next record is yielded for validation. The iterator has already consumed a second later record at that point. The passing balance-lookahead test observes only the first call to follows, which can be the oldest-first calculation.
findings.repro: Load four descending dates with amounts of £1 and file-order balances £10, £8, £7, £6. Observe ingest.follows and _Feed.__next__. The call follows(800, 100, 1000), which detects the broken balance on CSV line 2, occurs after CSV line 4 has been read. R2 permits reading through line 3 before checking line 2.

findings.claim: The parser can accept a record containing invalid UTF-8. DictReader collapses repeated blank headers before unreadable_cells inspects the row, so a clean cell under the last blank header overwrites a bad byte under the first.
findings.repro: Use header bytes `id,date,description,amount,balance,,\n` and record bytes `A,2026-01-01,STRIPE,1.00,1.00,\xe9,ok\n`, with \xe9 a literal byte. load_csv accepts A because the dict contains only the last blank-column value, `ok`. R2 requires checking the unreadable record when met and naming line 2.

findings.claim: An oversized opening-balance option escapes as a raw integer-formatting error on Python 3.11 or later with the default decimal digit limit. The importer tries to print the entire option before it can name the disagreement on the export line.
findings.repro: Import a CSV with one GBP row, Amount 1.00 and Balance 1.00, passing --opening-balance followed by 5,000 digits of 9. The implied opening is 0.00. Formatting the supplied value through src/cma/metrics.py:135–138 raises ValueError instead of MonzoImportError.
